items.name: Classic Mung Kitchari
steps: Rinse the rice and mung dal until the draining water is mostly clear; soak for 20 minutes and drain.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pot; bloom the cumin, ginger, and turmeric just until fragrant.
Add the drained grains; turn them through the spiced fat for one minute.
Pour in the water, add the rock salt, and bring to a lively boil; lower the heat and cook covered for 30–35 minutes.
Stir and lightly press the grains to a cohesive, spoon-soft texture; rest covered for five minutes before serving warm.
items.guidance: This soft rice-and-mung kitchari is balanced for regular use when appetite is steady. Vata: serve warm with a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor coriander or fennel and keep pungent seasoning mild. Kapha: use a lighter portion and sharpen gently with dry ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Hemanta Strength Bowl
steps: Rinse the urad dal and cracked wheat separately; soak both for 30 minutes and drain.
Warm half the ghee in a heavy pot and toast the drained wheat for two minutes.
Add the urad dal, dry ginger, and water; simmer covered until both grains are very soft.
Stir in the jaggery and remaining ghee only after the grains are cooked; continue until the bowl is cohesive.
Finish with crushed cardamom, rest covered, and serve warm in modest portions.
items.guidance: This substantial urad-and-wheat bowl reflects the building foods traditionally favored in early winter. Vata: serve warm and well cooked. Pitta: use less dry ginger and jaggery. Kapha: choose mung kitchari instead when lightness is preferred.

items.name: Grishma Cooling Plate
steps: Rinse and soak the rice for 15 minutes, then drain.
Cook the rice with the measured water until tender; rest covered for eight minutes and fluff gently.
Whisk the buttermilk with toasted cumin and half the rock salt.
Fold the cucumber and mint together with the remaining salt just before serving.
Arrange warm rice, the cucumber-mint portion, and buttermilk separately on each plate so diners combine small mouthfuls as desired.
items.guidance: Warm rice with cucumber, mint, and churned buttermilk makes a mild hot-season midday plate. Vata: keep the rice warm and reduce raw cucumber. Pitta: retain the mild seasoning and avoid chilies. Kapha: reduce rice and emphasize the diluted buttermilk.

items.name: Sharad Pitta-Soothing Bowl
steps: Rinse and soak the rice for 15 minutes, then drain.
Cook the rice with the water until tender; rest covered for eight minutes.
Warm the ghee with lightly crushed fennel and fold it through the rice.
Let the rice cool from hot to pleasantly warm, then scatter over the pomegranate and a very light dusting of rock sugar.
Serve at midday without pungent accompaniments.
items.guidance: This mild autumn bowl uses sweet, cooling accents and avoids pungent seasoning. Vata: serve the rice warmer and add a little ghee. Pitta: retain the gentle fennel and small sweet garnish. Kapha: omit the rock sugar and take a smaller rice portion.

items.name: Vasanta Kapha-Clearing Meal
steps: Rinse and soak the barley for 35 minutes, then drain.
Simmer the barley in the water until tender and separate; drain any excess water.
Warm the ghee, add the bitter gourd, dry ginger, pepper, and rock salt, and cook until tender with dry edges.
Arrange the warm barley and bitter gourd together, then let the plate cool until no longer hot.
Drizzle the raw honey lightly over the barley only after cooling below hot serving temperature.
items.guidance: Barley, bitter gourd, and restrained fat give this spring plate a deliberately light character. Vata: add a little ghee and cook the barley softer. Pitta: reduce pepper and omit honey if the bitter-sweet contrast is unwelcome. Kapha: retain the dry texture and small honey measure.

Stir and lightly press the grains to a cohesive, spoon-soft texture; rest covered for five minutes before serving warm.
items.guidance: Chana Dal Rice Kitchari is a soft one-pot grain-and-pulse preparation suited to a freshly cooked meal. Vata: serve warm with a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor coriander or fennel and keep pungent seasoning mild. Kapha: use a lighter portion and sharpen gently with dry ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Panchmel Rice Khichdi
steps: Rinse the rice and mixed dals until the draining water is mostly clear; soak for 40 minutes and drain.
Warm the ghee in a heavy pot; bloom the cumin, ginger, and turmeric just until fragrant.
Add the drained grains and the prepared red lentils, toor dal, chana dal, split urad dal, asafoetida; turn them through the spiced fat for one minute.
Pour in the water, add the rock salt, and bring to a lively boil; lower the heat and cook covered for 30–35 minutes.
Stir and lightly press the grains to a cohesive, spoon-soft texture; rest covered for five minutes before serving warm.
items.guidance: Panchmel Rice Khichdi is a soft one-pot grain-and-pulse preparation suited to a freshly cooked meal. Vata: serve warm with a little extra ghee. Pitta: favor coriander or fennel and keep pungent seasoning mild. Kapha: use a lighter portion and sharpen gently with dry ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Manda (Thin Rice Water)
steps: Rinse the rice thoroughly and place it in a deep pot with the measured water.
Bring to a boil, then cook at a gentle simmer until the grains are extremely soft and the liquid turns cloudy.
Pour through a fine strainer without pressing hard; reserve the thin, starchy liquid and discard or repurpose the grains.
Season the strained liquid lightly with rock salt and serve it warm in small bowls.
items.guidance: Manda is the strained, thinnest rice preparation in the classical gruel sequence. Vata: serve warm and optionally add a trace of ghee. Pitta: keep it plain and lightly salted. Kapha: take a small serving with dry ginger only if desired.

items.name: Peya (Thin Gruel)
steps: Rinse the rice well; soak for 15 minutes, then drain.
Bring the measured water to a boil and stir in the grain with sliced fresh ginger.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring from time to time, until the grains are broken and suspended in ample broth.
Add the rock salt, whisk briefly to even the texture, and serve warm without reheating repeatedly.
items.guidance: Peya (Thin Gruel) uses prolonged cooking and ample moisture for a gentle texture. Vata: take it warm and add ghee only if desired. Pitta: serve plain or with coriander. Kapha: keep the serving small and season with dry ginger.

items.name: Vilepi (Thick Gruel)
steps: Rinse the rice well; soak for 15 minutes, then drain.
Bring the measured water to a boil and stir in the grain.
Lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring from time to time, until the grains are very soft and the gruel holds a spoon trail.
Add the rock salt, whisk briefly to even the texture, and serve warm without reheating repeatedly.

items.name: Classical Mung Yusha
steps: Rinse the mung dal and soak it for 25 minutes; drain well.
Combine the pulse, turmeric, and water in a pot; bring to a boil and skim any foam from the surface.
Add cumin, and ginger; simmer until the pulse is completely tender.
Whisk the soup to loosen some of the cooked pulse while keeping the broth pourable, then add the rock salt.
Rest covered for three minutes and ladle into warm bowls.
items.guidance: Classical Mung Yusha is prepared as a pourable pulse broth rather than a heavy stew. Vata: add a small spoon of ghee at the table. Pitta: omit extra chilies and emphasize coriander. Kapha: increase dry spice modestly and keep the broth thin.
